title: Validation of InBody 770 bioelectrical impedance analysis compared to a four-compartment model criterion in young adults (Brewer et al. 2021)
content: Brewer GJ et al., 2021 — Compared the InBody 770 (BIA) against a four-compartment model (the gold-standard criterion) for body composition in young adults. InBody-derived body-fat percentage carried a total error of roughly 4.2 percentage points; fat mass and fat-free mass each carried a total error around 2.4 kg versus the criterion method. InBody/BIA readings should be treated as ESTIMATES with real measurement uncertainty, not exact values.

title: Validation of InBody 770 bioelectrical impedance analysis compared to a four-compartment model criterion in young adults (Brewer et al. 2021)
content: Brewer et al. 2021 — Product implication: a body-fat% change from, say, 24.0% to 25.0% on two InBody scans is well within this device's known measurement error band and must NOT be presented as a confirmed 1-percentage-point increase in true body fat. Small week-to-week InBody deltas should be described with appropriate uncertainty (e.g. 'estimated', 'within normal measurement variation') rather than as precise, confirmed facts, especially for a single pair of readings rather than a longer trend.
